newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: GEC-Marconi in new offset project in UAE.
newsitem.headline: GEC-Marconi in new offset project in UAE.

text.p: Britain's GEC-Marconi is taking a stake in a joint venture remote sensing company in the United Arab Emirates as part of its commitments under the UAE's offset programme, the joint venture partners said on Wednesday.

"The Gulf Centre for Remote Sensing is a joint venture between the Abu Dhabi Industrial Development Co (ADIDCO), the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) and GEC-Marconi," NRSC marketing director Tristram Cary told a news conference.
"This joint venture is being formed under the UAEoffsets programme," Cary said, adding it would be based in Abu Dhabi.

The private ADIDCO will have 51 percent and GEC-Marconi and NRSC 24.5 percent each, he said. The three firms will inject an initial total five million dirhams ($1.36 million) into the firm, which currently operates as a NRSC office in Dubai, another of the seven emirates that make up the UAE.

It will extract information from data collected by satellite or airborne sensors, which can then be used in environmental surveys, oil and gas exploration, crop growth and health analysis and pollution monitoring, Cary said.
GEC-Marconi has long-standing ties with Abu Dhabi.

Peter Cross, general manager of GEC-Marconi Offsets International in Abu Dhabi, declined to give the value of his company's offset commitment to the Gulf Arab state, but said the new venture was part of an existing offset obligation.
Under the terms of the UAE's offset scheme, international arms manufacturers supplying the UAE are required to invest a portion of a deal's worth in profitable ventures with a local partner.

Cross said GEC-Marconi had already set up the Gulf Solar Power company. It was also setting up a furniture manufacturing and interior contracting firm and has plans for a ship-owning joint venture which will charter out ships to a UAE operator.
"Many more projects are in the pipeline which illustrate our commitment to the UAE offset programme," he said.
NRSC is 45 percent owned by Matra Marconi -- a joint venture between GEC-Marconi and Matra. GEC-Marconi is part of Britain's General Electric Co.
Most of NRSC's clients in the Gulf are oil and gas industry players and municipalities, Cary said.
